evidence.summary: Seska's recorded message claims Culluh will take the newborn she describes as Chakotay's son; Chakotay separately processes the involuntary-DNA claim through a spiritual dream/vision of his father.
Chakotay states his DNA was taken and used by Seska to impregnate herself without his consent.
Tierna claims Seska was killed and the child taken, supplying navigation codes and details that partly withstand initial checks.
Repeated Kazon attacks focus on the same damaged sector, leading Voyager to suspect coordinated shaping of its route.
Kazon forces exploit Voyager's evasive choices and Tierna's deception; Tierna detonates himself as part of the trap.
Kazon overwhelm Voyager, board the ship, and capture the crew while Paris escapes in a shuttle seeking Talaxian help.
Culluh treats the baby as his own and reveals his understanding of the child's conception conflicts with what Seska told Chakotay.
The Kazon seize Voyager and strand its crew on a primitive planet with limited resources.
Suder practices meditation, develops horticultural work, accepts confinement, and asks for ways to contribute to Voyager.

assertions.subject: voy-b1:seska
counterevidence: Later medical evidence in Basics Part II contradicts Chakotay paternity.

assertions.subject: voy-b1:suder
counterevidence: Prior killings and confinement remain part of his record.

neutral_coding.plot_problem: A supposed rescue of Seska's child becomes a coordinated Kazon trap ending in Voyager's capture and crew marooning.
neutral_coding.epistemics: Seska's paternity/distress claims, Tierna's false account, Chakotay's vision, and verified attack behavior are separated.
neutral_coding.counterevidence: Initial corroboration of parts of Tierna's story does not make the whole account true; paternity remains contested pending later evidence.
